title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Appropriate Equipment & Instrumentation - Biotechnology - Micropipettes (first
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: When aspirating a $25 \ \mu\text{L}$ sample of buffer using a P200 micropipette, at what specific point in the procedure should the technician depress the plunger to the **first stop**?
options: Before submerging the pipette tip into the source liquid.
Immediately after submerging the pipette tip deep into the source liquid.
Only when attempting to expel the liquid into the destination tube.
After drawing the liquid up, to push out any accidentally trapped air bubbles.
questions.explain:
Correct pipetting technique requires depressing the plunger to the **first stop** (the point of initial resistance) *before* the tip enters the liquid. 

Pushing to the first stop displaces exactly the calibrated volume of air ($25 \ \mu\text{L}$ in this case). Once the tip is submerged, the plunger is slowly released, creating a vacuum that draws exactly $25 \ \mu\text{L}$ of liquid into the tip. If you depress the plunger *after* submerging (Option 'b'), you will blow air bubbles into the sample, which can cause foaming or spillover.

questions.q: During the dispensing phase of micropipetting, what is the specific mechanical purpose of depressing the plunger past the initial resistance point to the **second stop**?
options: To draw the precise target volume of liquid up into the tip.
To eject the contaminated plastic pipette tip directly into the biohazard waste bin.
To violently mix the contents of the destination tube by bubbling air through the solution.
To force a final blast of air through the tip, expelling any residual liquid clinging to the inside.
questions.explain:
The **second stop** on a micropipette is specifically designed for the "blow-out" phase. 

When dispensing, the technician depresses the plunger to the first stop, which pushes out the measured liquid. However, due to surface tension, a tiny droplet often remains inside the very end of the plastic tip. Pushing all the way down to the second stop forces a final surge of air through the tip, blowing out that last residual drop and ensuring the complete, accurate volume is delivered. 
> Option 'b' describes the tip ejector button, not the plunger.
